subtopics.title: The Cast of Symbols and the Two Kinds of Growth

questions.question: An interest rate of 8% per annum enters either growth formula as:
The essential difference between simple and compound growth is that:
options: Simple growth uses a higher rate
Compound growth only applies to banks
Simple interest is calculated on the principal only; compound interest is calculated on principal plus accumulated interest
Simple growth runs for fewer years

questions.question: In $A = P(1 + i)^n$, why is the bracket raised to the power $n$?
options: Because the growth factor is applied once per period, each time to an already-grown amount
It is a printing convention with no meaning

subtopics.title: Simple Growth — Executing A = P(1 + in)

questions.question: R5 000 at 8% per annum simple interest for 3 years accumulates to:
Inside the bracket of $A = 5\,000(1 + 0{,}08 \times 3)$, the correct computation order gives:
The fingerprint that verifies a simple-interest answer is:
options: The interest decomposes into equal annual payments calculated on the original principal
The answer is always a round number

subtopics.title: Compound Growth — Executing A = P(1 + i)ⁿ

questions.question: R5 000 at 8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years accumulates to:
Writing $A = 5\,000(1 + 0{,}08 \times 3)$ in a question that says 'compounded annually' is wrong because:
options: The principal is in the wrong place
It is the simple formula — under compounding, $n$ must be an exponent: $5\,000(1{,}08)^3$
Nothing is wrong — the two forms are equivalent

questions.question: The R98,56 gap between the compound and simple answers comes from:
options: Rounding the growth factor too early
A higher rate in the compound case
Interest earned by earlier interest: R32 extra in year two and R66,56 extra in year three

questions.question: When should the growth factor 1,259712 be rounded?
options: Only at the final answer, to two decimals for money
Rounding is never allowed in finance

subtopics.title: Choosing the Formula and Working Backwards

questions.question: By the CAPS convention, hire purchase is calculated with:
options: Either formula, at the shop's choice

questions.question: A TV costs R8 000 on hire purchase over 2 years at 12% p.a. simple interest. The total paid and monthly instalment are:
What principal must be invested at 6% compound interest to reach R10 000 in 4 years?
Which scenario list correctly pairs with COMPOUND growth?
options: Inflation, savings compounded annually, population growth

subtopics.title: Two Pictures — the Wage and the Taxi

questions.question: In the two pictures, the weekend wage stands for simple growth because:
options: The payment is calculated on the same original deal every time and never changes
The wage is paid weekly instead of yearly

questions.question: The taxi owner's money grows faster and faster because:
options: She works longer hours each year
The earnings are saved and start earning too — growth joins the team and works

questions.question: Which everyday situation matches the TAXI picture?
options: A fixed R400 pocket-money payment every month
A savings account where each year's interest is added to the balance
Paying the same taxi fare every morning
A shop marking one price down once

subtopics.title: The Same R5 000, Built Year by Year

questions.question: Built year by year at 8% compound, R5 000 becomes:
In year two of the compound build, the interest is R432 rather than R400 because:
options: 8% is now calculated on R5 400 — last year's R400 has joined the balance and earns too

questions.question: If you forget which formula is which in a test, the year-by-year build is valuable because:
options: It is faster than the formula
It reconstructs either answer from arithmetic you can always do — the formula is just this build in a hurry

subtopics.title: Which Deal Is in Front of You?

questions.question: 'A fridge bought on hire purchase over 30 months' is which deal?
options: The wage deal — simple interest on the original price
Neither — hire purchase has no interest

questions.question: Why is inflation a taxi-deal (compound) situation?
options: Because prices only rise in taxi fares
Because inflation is set by banks
Because each year's price rise happens on top of last year's already-risen prices
Because inflation uses a different rate every year

questions.question: The honest warning about compound growth is that:
options: It stops working after ten years
It works both ways — wonderful for savings you own, heavy for debts you owe
